page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-4 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The configuration includes 2 dedicated virtual CPUs mapping directly to 2 physical cores clocked at a fixed 3.6 GHz frequency, operating with a single thread per core. System memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The profile contains zero integrated local storage, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external block storage volumes for persistent data retention. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and contains no discrete graphics processing hardware. Because the execution units are dedicated rather than shared or hyperthreaded, core execution avoids thread-level resource contention, though workloads must be compatible with the ARM64 instruction set.

With its 1:2 compute-to-memory density and dedicated core allocation, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for execution patterns requiring predictable clock speeds without large memory overhead. The instance fits lightweight containerized applications, ARM64 build nodes, continuous integration runners, API gateways, and web application routing layers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-4 is a dual-core virtual server based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor running at 3.6 GHz, the system assigns 2 dedicated physical cores across 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring consistent compute execution. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local solid-state drives or GPUs are provisioned with this profile, requiring persistent file systems and databases to utilize attached network storage volumes. Network connectivity is supported with one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated single-thread-per-core topology and moderate memory allocation, VM.Standard.A4.Flex.1-4 is positioned for lightweight computational workloads, ARM-native application compilation, web serving, microservices, and continuous integration agents that do not require heavy in-memory data structures.
